concerns.text: The plan aborts if the FluorDB joint SMILES + FQY dataset is not in the verified‑datasets list. Since the dataset is currently unverified, the pipeline cannot run at all, making the entire research question unanswerable until a verified source is provided or the scope is changed.

concerns.location: plan.md:## Timeline (estimated on CI runner, assuming verified data is available) – Test‑set size
concerns.text: The scaffold split guarantees a test set of at least 20 molecules (FR‑013). Twenty points is far below what is needed for reliable regression evaluation (R², RMSE) and for bootstrap confidence intervals; the claimed half‑width ≤ 0.07 is based on a simplistic simulation and may be overly optimistic, risking under‑powered conclusions.

concerns.location: plan.md:## 7️⃣ Interpretability (Integrated Gradients & SHAP) – IG vs SHAP sanity‑check
concerns.text: Requiring Pearson ≥ 0.7 between IG and SHAP on only 30 random test molecules (three seeds) is a weak sanity‑check. With such a small sample the correlation estimate is noisy, and passing the threshold does not guarantee that attributions are chemically meaningful.

concerns.location: plan.md:## 8️⃣ Substructure Aggregation & Validation – overlap criteria
concerns.text: The validation step demands ≥ 12/20 overlap with a curated fluorophore‑motif set and > 1.5× enrichment over random. This criterion is arbitrary and may bias the interpretation; the reference set is pruned of any motif appearing in train or test, which can dramatically shrink the set and inflate overlap scores, confounding the claim of meaningful attribution.

Solvent, temperature, and measurement‑method metadata are concatenated to the model inputs, but the plan does not describe any analysis to assess or control for their confounding effect on FQY predictions or on attribution rankings, leaving a potential hidden confound.

concerns.location: plan.md:## 7️⃣ Interpretability (Integrated Gradients & SHAP) – IG vs SHAP sanity‑check
concerns.text: The plan treats the IG vs SHAP correlation as a pass/fail gate (abort if < 0.7). This binary decision does not account for statistical uncertainty of the correlation estimate and may cause unnecessary pipeline failures.
